title: Choking – Infant (under 1 year)
summary: For a baby who cannot cry, cough or breathe: back blows with the head lower than the chest, then chest thrusts. Never abdominal thrusts.

callEmergency.headline: Call {EMERGENCY} if the baby cannot cry, cough or breathe
when: Silent or ineffective cough, cannot cry or breathe
After the obstruction clears – the baby should still be checked

steps.title: Recognise severe choking
steps.text: Effective cough or crying: let the baby cough and watch closely. Cannot cry, cough or breathe: act now and get someone to call {EMERGENCY}.

steps.title: Up to 5 back blows
steps.text: Lay the baby face down along your forearm, head lower than the chest, supporting the head and jaw with your hand. Rest your arm on your thigh. Give up to 5 firm blows between the shoulder blades with the heel of your other hand.

steps.title: Up to 5 chest thrusts
steps.text: Turn the baby face up along your other forearm, head lower than the chest. Using two fingers or two thumbs on the lower half of the breastbone (as for infant CPR), give up to 5 chest thrusts, sharper and slower than CPR compressions.

steps.title: Keep alternating
steps.text: Repeat 5 back blows and 5 chest thrusts until the object comes out or the baby becomes unresponsive.

steps.title: If the baby becomes unresponsive
steps.text: Call {EMERGENCY} if not already done and start infant CPR. Look in the mouth before giving breaths and remove any object you can see.

warningSigns: Unable to cry or make sounds
doNot: Do not give abdominal thrusts to a baby
Do not hold the baby upside down by the legs
Do not do blind finger sweeps
